name: AI News
blurb: Daily AI news from the publishers who broke it, split into headline coverage of the field and vendor announcements from the companies building it. Every story links to the original source, and any claim quoted in our coverage is cross-referenced against the laws, lawsuits, companies, tools, papers, and people already tracked in this atlas.

domains.name: AI Headline News
domains.blurb: The day's most consequential AI stories across law, policy, research, safety, and society, curated from 34 vetted feeds. Each item carries the original publisher link and a note on how it connects to the bills, cases, and frameworks tracked elsewhere on this site.

domains.name: AI Vendor News
domains.blurb: Product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements from the AI vendors themselves. Each item links to the vendor's original announcement and cross-references the company's profile in our AI Companies directory where one exists.

domains.name: This Week in AI
domains.blurb: A weekly record of what moved in AI policy and litigation, permalinked by ISO week.

domains.name: AI Historical Timeline
domains.blurb: From the 1940s to the present: Turing, the perceptron, expert systems, backpropagation, deep learning, AlexNet, transformers, and what followed.

reading.body:
AI news coverage is almost entirely one stream: 524 of 540 pages are curated headline stories, while vendor announcements amount to a single page and the historical timeline holds none.

The imbalance is the pattern. Headline coverage is built out across law, policy, research, safety, and society, drawn from 34 vetted feeds, and every one of its 524 pages carries sections. Vendor news, which covers product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements, has one page. The weekly policy and litigation record has 15 pages, permalinked by ISO week. The historical timeline is marked live with zero pages, so a declared section exists without content behind it.

For AI specifically, the thin side is the commercially load-bearing one. Model releases, pricing changes, and capacity announcements arrive through vendor channels, and that is where claims about compute, datacenters, and power tend to originate. The headline stream is where the law and policy that govern those builds would surface, and it is the only stream with real depth. A reader can follow regulation and litigation here at length, and cannot follow the companies at comparable resolution.

What the data does not say is how much is inside any of it. There are no story counts, no date range, and no way to tell whether the single vendor page is a stub or a working index. The 15 weekly pages imply a bounded window without giving its start or end. The zero-page timeline may be unbuilt or unpublished, and the data cannot distinguish the two.
